title: Compact catalog card + quick-pin flow brainstorm
body:
Purpose: quick exploration of a compact model card UI and a one-click 'pin to endpoint' experience for power users. Focus: reduce cognitive load when scanning many models, give fast pin/preview actions, and make pin semantics explicit (pin vs deploy vs dry-run).

High-level constraints and goals:
- Cards must fit dense lists (4-6 columns on wide screens) while remaining scannable for model size, latency, and token cost.
- Primary action should be keyboard-accessible (Enter to open, P to pin, / to focus search).
- Pin flow needs clear indication of what gets pinned (model version, quantization variant, and config snapshot).
- Preserve rollback and automatic fallback explanations in microcopy.

Wireframe sketches (compact card) — vertical content order when in dense layout:
1) Model badge row: small logo (optional) | model name (bold) | version tag (inline)
2) Metadata chips: arch / params / default seq length / avg latency (ms)
3) Economics row: tokens-per-1000 / typical cost-per-1k / throughput (rps)
4) Quick-actions toolbar (icon-only): preview, pin, compare, metrics
5) Overflow: elipsis open full action menu with: pin+create-endpoint, pin-to-route, view-detailed-profile

Behavior notes:
- Hover state: expand card to show copy of first-line model description and 'fast preview' CTA.
- Keyboard: Tab focuses successive interactive elements; pressing 'p' while card focused opens pin modal.
- Tooltip microcopy: for 'pin' -> "Pin this model version to an endpoint configuration (saves model + variant + sampling)."

Pin modal (one-step optimistic flow) — draft copy and UX:
- Title: "Pin model to endpoint"
- Subtitle (muted): "This creates a named reference to the model version and snapshot of the chosen variant. You can use this pin in routes and deploy it later."
- Fields (compact): Pin name (auto-suggest from model + version), Variant (dropdown: fp16 / int8 / quant-llm), Default max_tokens (numeric), Traffic policy preview (defaults to 'none' until assigned)
- Primary CTA: "Create pin and copy ID" (secondary: "Create pin & open endpoint wizard")
- Small note below CTAs (muted): "Pins are non-destructive — you can update the underlying endpoint to use a different pin or roll back to an earlier pin. Pins do not allocate capacity by themselves."
- Danger/confirm copy when pin variant uses experimental quantization: "Experimental variant — outputs may differ. Use canary traffic for production rollouts."

Microcopy experiments (variations to test in A/B):
- Primary CTAs: ["Create pin", "Save pin", "Create pin (no deploy)"]
- Subtitle alternatives: ["A reusable reference to this model + config.", "Lock this version for use in routes and rollouts."]
- Tooltip for 'Create pin & open endpoint wizard': "Create the pin and take it straight to deployment settings."

Error and fallback language (short, actionable):
- If pin creation fails due to naming conflict: "A pin with that name already exists. Choose a new name or append -1 to reuse."
- If variant unsupported for selected endpoint: "Selected variant incompatible with endpoint runtime. Try a compatible variant or create a new endpoint runtime."

Accessibility considerations:
- ARIA label for pin button: "Pin model <model name> version <v>"
- Ensure high contrast in dense cards and that expanded hover previews are dismissible via Esc key.
- Provide full-text copy of metrics for screen readers; the compact card should not hide critical text behind hover-only states.

Edge scenarios and UX decisions to finalize:
- Pin semantics: should a pin be immutable (snapshot) or mutable (pointer)? Proposal: pin is a snapshot of model+variant+config but can be renamed; underlying model version remains fixed. Endpoint references a pin id. For quick rollouts we also allow 'pin alias' that points to a mutable redirect (future).
- Quick comparison flow: allow selecting checkboxes on cards and keyboard 'C' to open a side-by-side diff of latency, cost, and sample output.
- Multi-pin flow: when user pins from search results with multiple selections, open a compact batch-create modal.

Backlog (priority + short acceptance criteria):
- UX-1 (P0): compact card layout responsive up to 6 columns; CTA icon set, keyboard navigation. Acceptance: keyboard P opens pin modal, tab order validated. Jira: ENG-8742
- UX-2 (P1): one-step optimistic pin modal with copyable ID. Acceptance: created pin returns ID and shows toast with actions. Jira: UX-1290
- UX-3 (P1): microcopy A/B test for primary CTA wording for pin modal. Acceptance: run experiment for 2 weeks, track conversion to endpoint creation. Jira: EXP-44
- UX-4 (P2): accessibility audit and add ARIA labels for all interactive elements. Acceptance: pass internal a11y checklist. Jira: ACCESS-77

Prototype interactions to include in next build:
- Dense grid toggle in user preferences to test scanning speed vs detail preferences.
- 'P' keyboard shortcut hint in status bar when card list is focused.
- Quick preview: small ephemeral iframe with sample generation using a canned prompt (privacy-safe; uses sandboxed request).

Open questions for PM/Eng:
- Do we want pins to be visible across org by default or scoped to team? (security/privacy implications)
- API surface: should client get back pin metadata (created_by, variant, locked=true) in same call as pin create? recommended for console UX to avoid extra fetches.
- Telemetry: what events do we need? pin_create, pin_create_from_card, pin_open_wizard, pin_create_variant_experimental.

Copy snippets for testing (button/labels/alerts):
- Pin button (compact): "Pin" (aria: "Pin model")
- Pin tooltip: "Create a reusable reference to this model version."
- Toast success: "Pin created — ID copied to clipboard" / secondary action: "Open endpoint wizard"
- Error toast: "Pin not created — try again or contact support (link)"

Next steps (owners + dates):
- High-fidelity mockups (Priya) — due 2025-03-10
- Small prototyping PR (Ethan) — due 2025-03-24
- Product review + decision on pin immutability (Sofia) — agenda for 2025-03-05 weekly product sync

Notes to reviewers: this doc explores a fast path for experienced users (power scanning + keyboard shortcuts) while trying to keep the pin concept explicit for less experienced users. Looking to validate: (1) do we prefer optimistic single-step pin creation vs a two-step deploy concept, and (2) is microcopy clear about pin not provisioning capacity?
